'''''Mammillaria hahniana''''', the '''old lady cactus''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Cactaceae, [[native plant|native]] to central Mexico. It grows to {{convert|25|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall by {{convert|50|cm|0|abbr=on}} broad. The solitary spherical stems, 12 cm in diameter, are covered in white down and white spines. Reddish purple flowers are borne in spring and summer, sometimes forming a complete ring around the apex of the plant.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1-4053-3296-5|pages=1136}}</ref>

Its status is listed as "Near Threatened" by the IUCN Red List.<ref name="iucn status 12 November 2021" />
==Cultivation==
''Mammillaria hahniana'' is one of several ''Mammillaria'' species to be cultivated. In [[temperateness|temperate]] regions it must be grown under glass with heat. However, some growers report that it is quite hardy down to {{convert|-5 |C|F|abbr=on}} or even {{convert| -10|C|F|abbr=on}}. Like all cacti it must be kept dry in winter, and fed and watered during the active growth cycle in summer. Increasing quite readily and flowering at a relatively early age, it is a suitable subject for domestic cultivation.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.llifle.com/Encyclopedia/CACTI/Family/Cactaceae/22358/Mammillaria_hahniana
| title = ''Mammillaria hahniana'' Werd. | publisher = Encyclopedia of Cacti | access-date = 3 April 2018}}</ref> It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Mammillaria hahniana''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/10821/mammillaria-hahniana/details | access-date = 3 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 63 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 3 April 2018}}</ref>
